stem: A biased coin has probability 1/3 of showing heads on each toss. If the coin is tossed 4 times, what is the probability of getting exactly 2 heads?

per_option_rationale.rationale: 4/81 = (1/3)^2*(2/3)^2 without the combination C(4,2)=6; the student applied the probability of one specific sequence instead of summing over all C(4,2) arrangements.
6/81 = C(4,2)*(1/3)^4 = 6/81; the student replaced both the success and failure probabilities with p=1/3, ignoring q=2/3 in the failure factor.
32/81 = C(4,1)*(1/3)^1*(2/3)^3 = 4*(1/3)*(8/27) = 32/81; the student applied the binomial formula for k=1 instead of k=2, computing P(X=1) rather than P(X=2).

explanation_sections.punchline: With p != 1/2 both the success probability (1/3)^2 and the failure probability (2/3)^2 must appear; the combination C(4,2)=6 must also be included.
explanation_sections.lesson: The Binomial formula has three factors: the combination C(n,k), p^k, and q^(n-k); all three must be present.
explanation_sections.timing: 60 seconds. Work in fractions: 6*(1/9)*(4/9)=24/81. Eliminate option 2 (omits q^2) and option 1 (omits C(4,2)) first.
